status.label: Related transient-window fix under review
status.detail: Open PR #51162 changes the same new-window restoration path for a traced 3ds Max case; TickTick coverage remains unverified.

next_action.label: Test TickTick against related fix
next_action.reason: Reuse the concrete active fix attempt instead of inventing assigned ownership or a competing implementation.

judgment.rationale: A concrete open fix attempt addresses the same suspected transient-window restoration mechanism, so parallel implementation is not warranted before testing applicability. This issue is not claimed fixed or duplicated by #51161.
evidence: Disabling 'Move newly created windows to their last known zone' prevents the TickTick blank-window symptom; upgrading to 0.65.0 did not solve it.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/33255 was closed as a duplicate of #22515.

https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/51161 presents WinEvent traces of a transient 3ds Max window re-shown by asynchronous SW_RESTORE and explicitly identifies TickTick as a possible related family.

https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/51162 is open and queues new windows for a 100 ms settle period before the existing WindowCreated checks; its reported E2E validation is for 3ds Max, not TickTick.
judgment.recommended_action: Validate TickTick with the related fix candidate, retaining this issue until its own reproduction is verified.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open PR #51162 is an existing fix attempt for the shared candidate new-window/async-restore path, with a concrete public reproduction in #51161. Coverage of TickTick is a hypothesis requiring a separate A/B test; it is not a shipped fix or confirmed resolution of #22515.

issue_context.summary: TickTick can open an immovable white extra window when FancyZones restores newly created windows to their previous zones. Disabling restoration or launching TickTick before PowerToys avoids the symptom.
known_information: TickTick 4.3.4.0 and PowerToys 0.64.1 were initially reported; the author confirmed persistence on 0.65.0.
Several contributors reproduced the problem, including on Windows 11.
The setting-off workaround and application-startup-order workaround are already documented.
The issue is open and has no assignees; related PR #51162 is open.
inferences: TickTick may briefly expose a helper window that gets restored after being hidden, like the traced 3ds Max case, but no TickTick-specific trace proves it.
issue_context.analysis: Replace the false empty-assignee ownership statement with real linked work and an explicit coverage limitation. Preserve the original issue as a validation target rather than declaring it solved.
initial_investigation: Read the original report and all eight comments.
Inspected cross-referenced #33255, #51161 and the full #51162 PR description, state and changed-file list.
Verified current upstream WindowUtils uses asynchronous SetWindowPlacement and SW_RESTORE; PR #51162 targets the new-window timing boundary without claiming TickTick E2E evidence.

reproduce.title: TickTick startup-window A/B validation
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare a current released build with an isolated build containing PR #51162; record the exact candidate commit.
prerequisites: Test build deployment follows the normal module-validation workflow; do not replace a user's working installation without preserving it.
steps: 1. Enable 'Move newly created windows to their last known zone', snap TickTick, close it and cold-start it repeatedly while PowerToys is already running.
2. Record main/helper window visibility and zone placement; compare with the setting disabled.
3. Repeat the same sequence with PR #51162's candidate, tracing show/hide and restore ordering if a white window remains.
4. Verify the normal TickTick window still restores to its zone and unrelated applications do not lose restoration.
reproduce.expected_result: No extra immovable white window, with normal main-window zone restoration retained. If TickTick still fails, record that the related fix does not cover this reproduction.
